thread:
helena (oncall): heads up — we just started getting a wave of 5xxs for /v1/generate across hosted-prod in us-west-2. Customer tickets coming in. I see a canary rollout from 10m ago. Can SRE/Runtime take a look?

oncall-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for service=redwood-api route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 pct_5xx=7.2% > threshold 2% (10m). Related alerts: increased error budget burn, latency spike.

raj: looking at runtime logs now. initial suspicion: canary that touched batching/orch matrix flags. I'm seeing upstream 502 from gateway proxy to inference-pool.

luis: pulling LB and gateway metrics. There's a surge in connection resets and a bunch of 504s from proxy->runtime. No host flaps.

sophie: that canary was the matrix-flag toggle (matrix_batching_v2) rolled to 10% 12m ago. I didn't see immediate red flags in canary metrics on staging. Rolling to 10% on prod was manual.

emily-cs: several support tickets reporting timeouts and intermittent 500s, especially for requests with long prompt lengths. One customer noted errors only when using a specific model variant.

raj: grabbing logs filtered by request id from support ticket sample: ```
2025-11-18T21:12:03Z ERROR gateway proxy->runtime code=502 msg="upstream response invalid" request_id=ryq-3k2b
2025-11-18T21:12:03Z WARN runtime shard=pool-7 kv_cache_miss=true seq_len=4096 latency_ms=1200
2025-11-18T21:12:04Z ERROR runtime oom_guard=true module=batcher reason="request dropped" request_id=ryq-3k2b
```

raj: that oom_guard log is weird — we haven't seen request drops at 10% canary before. Could be batching matrix producing oversized batching windows and then eviction.

luis: I can see increased queue depth on some dedicated worker pools that the canary touched. Simpler routing may be causing mismatched worker assignment.

sophie: the canary changed two config keys: matrix_batching_v2=true and route_rewrite_priority=runtime-first. We also flipped model_variant_priority to prefer quantized-variants for cost.

mikaela: @sophie — can you confirm the canary scope? Did the change apply to only a subset of customers or everyone with model=redwood-1-large?

sophie: scope was tag:canary-2025-11-18 applied to 10% traffic for model=redwood-1-large and model_variant=*quantized*. So yes it targeted quantized variants.

emily-cs: one paying customer noted billing anomalies (requests retried) and wants an ETA. They are escalated.

raj: repro attempt: curling hosted endpoint with long prompt + prefer_quantized header produced timeouts locally when routed through canary nodes. Minimal repro: ````bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Prefer-Variant: quantized" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"<~4k tokens>"}' -v --max-time 30
````

raj: reproduces a 504 after ~25s. Stack trace on runtime shows batcher waiting for prefix K/V while runtime-first routing waits on variant translation. It's a deadlock-ish pattern with large seq_len.

luis: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale up worker pool for affected shard, 2) rollback the canary flag to 0% for matrix_batching_v2, 3) enable fallback route to stable batching. Which do we want now?

helena (oncall): prioritize immediate customer impact — rollback the canary for matrix_batching_v2 and enable fallback routing. I'll coordinate deploy. @deploy-bot can you run the flag rollback to 0% and set route_rewrite_priority back to default?

deploy-bot: ACCEPTED: Initiating rollback job id=rb-2150001234. Commander=sophie. Starting flag revert: matrix_batching_v2 -> false for tag:canary-2025-11-18.

ops-automation-bot: NOTE: TTL for rollback script is 300s. Will also post an event to incident timeline.

mikaela: quick check — will rollback impact current in-flight requests? Expectation: new requests will avoid canary nodes, in-flight will finish; but we may still see residual errors for queued long requests.

raj: confirmed: after flag flip traffic sample to canary nodes dropped to <1% within 45s. Error rate from /v1/generate down to 1.1% after 2m. Gateway 504s reduced.

luis: scaled up pool for shard pool-7 by +3 instances as temporary buffer. Queue depth normalized. No further OOM logs.

emily-cs: update to customers: sent templated note — apologizing, explaining transient routing regression during canary, rollback completed, ask to reopen if they still see errors.

sophie: note — I misread the matrix flag interactions. On staging the routing priority was different (we had route-level fallback) — that didn't carry to prod due to a missing default mapping. My bad.

helena (oncall): good catch. We'll run a quick smoke for long sequence prompts and quantized variants. Raj, can you run the regression test harness?

raj: running harness now. Tests: 50 long-seq requests against quantized variants. All passed at 30s timeout locally after rollback. Collecting traces.

mikaela: logging task: create a dashboard panel for matrix_batching_v2 -> worker_queue_depth and kv_cache_miss to catch earlier next time.

luis: creating an autoscaling tweak ticket to raise the pool target when queue depth > 200 for 2m. TT-1248.

helena (oncall): escalation closure steps: - rollback confirmed - scale buffer added - customer comms sent - create postmortem and action items (dashboard, autoscale, default route fallback)

ops-automation-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: incident_id=INC-2150001234 severity=high duration=5m6s. Summary: canary config + route priority change caused excessive batching behavior for long sequences -> increased 5xx/504s. Rollback and scaling mitigated.

mikaela: tagging for postmortem: owners=eng-runtime (raj), eng-sre (luis), product (sophie). Will schedule the writeup.

emily-cs: closing ticket batch for customers impacted and issuing credits where appropriate.

helena (oncall): thanks everyone. After postmortem, let's add a canary gating check for interactions between matrix_batching_v2 and route_rewrite_priority — maybe an automated canary regression that runs long-sequence load against targeted variants before any prod flag flip.

sophie: agreed. Also adding a pre-rollout checklist: ensure fallback mappings present in prod and validate variant routing matrix.

raj: I'll attach the trace snippets and the minimal repro commands to the postmortem doc. Repro steps included above.

mikaela: putting this thread as reference for the postmortem draft.

helena (oncall): incident clear. If any new errors pop, re-open channel. :white_check_mark:
